record.paper_title: An update on Weihrauch complexity, and some open questions
record.context_brief: False statements in extended Weihrauch degrees
record.original_question: What are examples of interesting extended Weihrauch degrees of false statements, and how do those degrees relate to the usual scaffold of standard Weihrauch degrees?

evidence.quote: Open Question 20. What are some examples of interesting extended Weihrauch degrees of false statements, and how do they relate to the usual scaffolding Weihrauch degrees?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Weihrauch reducibility compares multi-valued functions on represented spaces: for partial multi-valued functions f, g :⊆ N^N ⇒ N^N, one writes f ≤_W g if there exist computable functions H, K :⊆ N^N → N^N such that, whenever p is a name for an instance of f, K(p) is a name for an instance of g, and whenever q is a name for a g-solution to that instance, H⟨p, q⟩ is a name for an f-solution. The induced equivalence classes are the (standard) Weihrauch degrees, and they form an extensively studied lattice used to calibrate the uniform computational content of mathematical theorems.

Bauer's extended Weihrauch degrees enlarge this structure by representing problems as relations (or predicates) on Baire space rather than as multi-valued functions; in this larger structure one can also assign a degree to "problems" that have no solutions at all, including formal counterparts of false mathematical statements. The standard Weihrauch degrees embed into the extended Weihrauch degrees in a natural way, and the extended structure contains additional degrees corresponding to such empty/false problems.

Problem. Exhibit explicit and mathematically natural examples of extended Weihrauch degrees that arise from false statements (i.e. problems with empty solution set, or that otherwise fail to be realized by any function), and determine how these degrees sit relative to the embedded scaffold of standard Weihrauch degrees: identify their position with respect to standard benchmark degrees (such as the degrees of LPO, LLPO, choice principles C_N, C_{N^N}, WKL, lim, etc.), describe their behaviour under the lattice and algebraic operations (join, meet, product, parallelization, composition), and characterize structural features that distinguish "false" extended Weihrauch degrees from those induced by genuine multi-valued functions.
artifact.status_search_result: No source found that resolves this question. Recent work (e.g., a 2025 preprint constructing a topos for extended Weihrauch degrees, and work on instance reducibility) further develops the framework of extended Weihrauch degrees but does not appear to give a classification or natural catalogue of degrees corresponding to false statements relative to the standard Weihrauch scaffold. The question therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A topos for extended Weihrauch degrees
status_evidence.snippet: Recent categorical work develops a tripos/topos-theoretic framework for extended Weihrauch degrees, generalizing standard Weihrauch reducibility.
status_evidence.claim: The framework of extended Weihrauch degrees is still under active development, with no classification of 'false-statement' degrees provided.

status_evidence.title: Instance reducibility and Weihrauch degrees
status_evidence.snippet: Studies instance reducibility, related to Bauer's extended Weihrauch reducibility, but does not catalogue extended degrees of false statements.
status_evidence.claim: The relation between extended Weihrauch degrees of false statements and the standard Weihrauch scaffold is not addressed conclusively.
